levels.title: Target Lock
levels.story: The outpost scanner sees everyone, including harmless wanderers. Tell it exactly which zombies the net should catch.

scenarios.title: First signal
scenarios.objective: Select every runner zombie. Return an id column; the nets fire only at returned IDs.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Inspect both tables and identify the values the objective describes.
Use WHERE to filter rows.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE kind = 'runner'
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE kind = 'runner'

scenarios.title: Protect the canal
scenarios.objective: Select all zombies in the canal zone, regardless of kind. Return an id column.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Read the zone column before choosing a predicate.
Use WHERE zone = 'canal'.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE zone = 'canal';
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE zone = 'canal';

scenarios.title: Prioritize the threat
scenarios.objective: Select every zombie with a threat score of at least 3. Return an id column.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: The comparison must include the threshold itself.
Use >= rather than >.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE threat >= 3;
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE threat >= 3;

levels.title: Open the Gate
levels.story: The garden gate asks for an access code but never hears back. Repair both halves of its request journey.

scenarios.title: First signal
scenarios.objective: Connect the complete flow shown by the port labels.
scenarios.explanation: Every lookup needs a return path. A one-way audit sink cannot answer a request.
hints: Select an output port, then a matching input. Requests and responses are different signals.
Every required event needs its own path. Cache writes need invalidation; render events must settle.
gate.send → service.in; service.read → store.in; store.out → service.data; service.out → gate.receive

events.label: Request reaches storage and the result returns to the gate

scenarios.title: A proxy in the middle
scenarios.objective: Route the gate request through its proxy and return the storage response all the way to the gate.
scenarios.explanation: Every lookup needs a return path. A one-way audit sink cannot answer a request.
hints: Select an output port, then a matching input. Requests and responses are different signals.
Every required event needs its own path. Cache writes need invalidation; render events must settle.
gate.send → proxy.in; proxy.send → service.in; service.read → store.in; store.out → service.data; service.out → proxy.data; proxy.return → gate.receive

events.label: Request and response through the gate proxy

scenarios.title: A receipt for every gate opening
scenarios.objective: Route the gate request through its proxy and return the storage response all the way to the gate. Deliver a separate receipt to the audit log; never route the original request there.
scenarios.explanation: Every lookup needs a return path. A one-way audit sink cannot answer a request.
hints: Select an output port, then a matching input. Requests and responses are different signals.
Every required event needs its own path. Cache writes need invalidation; render events must settle.
gate.send → proxy.in; proxy.send → service.in; service.read → store.in; store.out → service.data; service.out → proxy.data; proxy.return → gate.receive; proxy.receipt → receipt.in

levels.title: First Outpost
levels.story: A hundred survivors share a small repair outpost. Build enough infrastructure for their actual traffic, within the outpost’s budget.

scenarios.title: Keep it small
scenarios.objective: Handle 5 requests/sec within 20 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. There is no service-redundancy requirement. Failure check: none.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
A single API is sufficient here; extra infrastructure costs budget.
Use client → API 1 → database.

scenarios.title: Even small outposts need uptime
scenarios.objective: Handle 15 requests/sec within 32 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. Keep redundant APIs and survive the listed failures. Failure check: api-1.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
The small request rate fits one API, but the outage requires two behind a health-checking balancer.
One solution: client, database, proxy, api-1, api-2. Connect the balancer to each API and each API to the selected database.

scenarios.title: The visiting repair fleet
scenarios.objective: Handle 65 requests/sec within 32 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. There is no service-redundancy requirement. Failure check: none.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
One API serves 40/sec. The 65/sec burst needs two, even though the population is still small.
One solution: client, database, proxy, api-1, api-2. Connect the balancer to each API and each API to the selected database.

levels.title: Threat Scanner
levels.story: The scanner has incomplete shield records. Build a predicate that handles unknown values and mixed threats correctly.

scenarios.title: First signal
scenarios.objective: Select zombies with threat at least 3 and an unknown shield.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Inspect both tables and identify the values the objective describes.
Use IS NULL for unknown values. Parenthesize OR groups before combining them with AND.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE threat >= 3 AND shield IS NULL
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE threat >= 3 AND shield IS NULL

scenarios.title: New conditions
scenarios.objective: Select runners or armored zombies with threat at least 2.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Inspect both tables and identify the values the objective describes.
Use IS NULL for unknown values. Parenthesize OR groups before combining them with AND.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE (kind = 'runner' OR kind = 'armored') AND threat >= 2
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE (kind = 'runner' OR kind = 'armored') AND threat >= 2

scenarios.title: Mastery challenge
scenarios.objective: Select zombies in the garden or tower with zero or unknown shields.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Inspect both tables and identify the values the objective describes.
Use IS NULL for unknown values. Parenthesize OR groups before combining them with AND.
SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE zone IN ('garden', 'tower') AND (shield = 0 OR shield IS NULL)
scenarios.solution: SELECT id FROM zombies WHERE zone IN ('garden', 'tower') AND (shield = 0 OR shield IS NULL)

levels.title: Cache Canal
levels.story: Canal sensors keep asking for the same target map. Restore their cache without serving yesterday’s positions.

scenarios.title: One cold read, one warm read
scenarios.objective: Connect the cold miss path, populate the cache, and return a warm hit without a database read.
scenarios.explanation: Cache-aside reads storage after a miss and fills the cache. Writes must invalidate the affected cached value before later reads can trust it.
hints: Select an output port, then a matching input. Requests and responses are different signals.
Every required event needs its own path. Cache writes need invalidation; render events must settle.
api.read → cache.read; cache.hit → api.hit; cache.miss → api.miss; api.load → db.read; db.out → api.data; api.fill → cache.fill

events.label: Cold read: miss, load, then populate
Warm read: return cached data without storage

scenarios.title: A changed target position
scenarios.objective: Connect the cold miss path, populate the cache, and return a warm hit without a database read. A write changes the target position; invalidate its cached value.
scenarios.explanation: Cache-aside reads storage after a miss and fills the cache. Writes must invalidate the affected cached value before later reads can trust it.

api.read → cache.read; cache.hit → api.hit; cache.miss → api.miss; api.load → db.read; db.out → api.data; api.fill → cache.fill; api.invalidate → cache.invalidate

scenarios.objective: Connect the cold miss path, populate the cache, and return a warm hit without a database read. A write changes the target position; invalidate its cached value. Also invalidate zone occupancy after evacuation. Leave the unrelated weather key alone.
scenarios.explanation: Cache-aside reads storage after a miss and fills the cache. Writes must invalidate the affected cached value before later reads can trust it.

scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
The balancer needs enough healthy API capacity after one API fails. Connect each API to storage.

scenarios.title: Uneven service capacity

levels.title: Mixed Horde
levels.story: The tower stores evacuation data separately from sightings. Join the records so the defenses only enter cleared zones.

scenarios.title: First signal
scenarios.objective: Select zombies with threat at least 2 in evacuated zones. Join zones to zombies so occupied shelters stay safe.
scenarios.explanation: SQL selects rows by their values. Equivalent SELECT queries are accepted; the unique id set determines which zombies are targeted.
hints: Inspect both tables and identify the values the objective describes.
Join zombies.zone to zones.name and filter evacuated = 1.
SELECT z.id FROM zombies AS z JOIN zones AS a ON z.zone = a.name WHERE a.evacuated = 1 AND z.threat >= 2

levels.title: Command Loop
levels.story: Two control screens disagree about the tower state. Connect commands and rendering so updates settle instead of echoing forever.

scenarios.title: One state owner
scenarios.objective: Connect the user command to state and render state back into the view. Rendering must not emit another command.
scenarios.explanation: Bidirectional binding has distinct command and render paths. Programmatic rendering must not re-emit a user command.
hints: Select an output port, then a matching input. Requests and responses are different signals.
Every required event needs its own path. Cache writes need invalidation; render events must settle.
view.input → state.update; state.render → view.render

events.label: Primary edit settles in all subscribed views

scenarios.title: Two-way editing, one state
scenarios.objective: Both control views may edit the same state. An edit in either view must update both views without an echo.
scenarios.explanation: Bidirectional binding has distinct command and render paths. Programmatic rendering must not re-emit a user command.

levels.title: Restore the Signal
levels.story: The whole city is listening. Scale the signal service, keep targeting data fresh, and carry traffic through the final outage.

scenarios.title: Wake the signal tower
scenarios.objective: Handle 12,000 requests/sec within 48 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. Keep redundant APIs and survive the listed failures. Failure check: api-1. Read reuse is 94%. Cached targeting data must stay fresh after writes.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
The balancer needs enough healthy API capacity after one API fails. Connect each API to storage.
One solution: client, database, proxy, api-1, api-2, api-3, cache. Connect the balancer to each API and each API to the selected database.

scenarios.title: Lower reuse, faster storage
scenarios.objective: Handle 15,000 requests/sec within 56 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. Keep redundant APIs and survive the listed failures. Failure check: api-1. Read reuse is 65%. Cached targeting data must stay fresh after writes.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
At 65% reuse, misses overload the original database even with caching. Compare the expanded storage tier against the budget.
One solution: client, database-fast, proxy, api-1, api-2, api-3, cache. Connect the balancer to each API and each API to the selected database.

scenarios.title: Stay fresh through a cache outage
scenarios.objective: Handle 18,000 requests/sec within 73 cost units and 80 ms modeled latency. Keep redundant APIs and survive the listed failures. Failure check: api-1, cache. Read reuse is 94%. Cached targeting data must stay fresh after writes.
scenarios.explanation: Capacity follows request rate, not population. A load balancer distributes traffic to healthy APIs. Cache hits reduce database reads, but API capacity and write freshness still matter.
hints: Place clients, APIs and a database. Connect the request path. All numbers are assumptions for this scenario.
A cache outage sends every read to storage. Provision a database that can carry the fallback traffic; a high-capacity design may also pass without a cache.
One solution: client, database-fast, proxy, api-1, api-2, api-3, cache. Connect the balancer to each API and each API to the selected database.
